jbtxHHpX_u0.title: 20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying
jbtxHHpX_u0.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
jbtxHHpX_u0.summary: In '20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying' (published 27 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA argues Meta's new Muse personal AI agent is the first real killer app for agentic AI — bringing agents to consumer spending — and maps the ~20 stocks it upends. He likes PayPal (bought back at ~$50 after the takeover-offer rejection cratered it; ~10x P/E vs 16x a year ago, stablecoin growth) and Shopify (Muse users find its merchants' products and check out via Shop Pay; the rails underneath if Muse becomes shopping's front door) as the 'winners to buy'. Expedia is a conditional rebound play: its Muse partnership could redirect bookings through Expedia at Booking's expense, and the stock trades at 16x earnings vs a 25x average — though he stays cautious on the whole travel-middleman group (TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Booking, -15% to -24% in a month). On the AI-build side he ranks four neo-clouds — Oracle, Nebius, CoreWeave, IREN — and takes another look only at Nebius (his pick): ~500% revenue growth, best debt-to-free-cash-flow (-1.8x), 9.8x growth-adjusted P/S — while flagging Oracle's force majeure on a 2.5GW New Mexico data center as 'the first crack in the entire AI boom'. He avoids brokerages (Schwab, Raymond James, LPL, Ameriprise), banks (BofA, JPMorgan) and insurers (Progressive, Allstate) — AI agents could replace advice fees and erode sticky deposit-sweep profits — plus subscription names exposed to AI-driven cancellations (Adobe, SiriusXM, Match, Peloton, Planet Fitness, crushed 15%). Meta itself he holds: great story but ~30% above its 5-year average valuation after the 30% three-week run. Other tickers discussed with no call: Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AppLovin, Amazon. Caption note: auto-captions garble 'CoreWeave' as 'Corvus', 'IREN' as 'Iron', and 'Marvell' as 'Marvel'; tickers here are corrected.

7Lm8O0CuvLs.title: AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!
7Lm8O0CuvLs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
7Lm8O0CuvLs.summary: In 'AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!' (published 29 Sep 2026), Jose Najarro covers two big semiconductor headlines. First, Nvidia increased its share-repurchase authorization by $150 billion, bringing the remaining buyback program to $235 billion to be executed through fiscal 2028 — against barely $100 billion of buybacks over the past decade. He reads it as a major confidence signal: management believes the money will be worth much more in the future, and the stock trades at roughly 19x forward earnings (likely 16-17x, he argues, since analysts keep underestimating Nvidia's growth). He also covers Nvidia's open agent safety platform — an open-source OpenShell runtime plus a Sentry watchdog running on Bluefield 4 DPUs — and notes partners include Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity, with OpenAI conspicuously absent. He reports Anthropic has contracted 2.6 gigawatts of Nvidia AI infrastructure to date, with partner contracted value exceeding $180 billion, dismissing fears Anthropic is moving away from Nvidia. Second, AMD's $8.2 billion all-stock acquisition of World Labs, the AI model and research lab founded by AI pioneer Dr. Fei-Fei Li (auto-captions garble her name as 'FFly'/'Dr. Lee'), expected to close by end of 2026. He frames it as a talent acquisition that gives AMD a front-row view of how AI workloads are evolving, informing its hardware/software roadmap and potential moves into robotics and physical AI. He applauds the all-stock structure — less than 1% of the company — as smarter than spending cash, while flagging one worry: AMD is already juggling software-stack improvements (ROCm), the Helios ramp, and a full-stack build-out, so this is one more thing on the plate. He trusts Lisa Su's judgment and expects the deal to look obviously smart in a year or two. Calls: NVDA — BUY (excited as an investor; buyback confidence; cheap forward P/E; $5T market cap noted); AMD — BUY (smart talent grab, trusts management; ~$67 per garbled captions). Other tickers discussed without calls: INTC and ARM (as compute platforms for the agent safety runtime), META (as an AMD partner), plus non-tradeable OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity.

gkt3BnXJf9s.summary: Joseph Hogue, CFA — 'My New Favorite Stocks for AI Growth AND Income' (published 29 Sep 2026). Pitch: income investors no longer have to choose between AI-driven growth and cash flow. Hogue argues new YieldMax option-income ETFs let holders capture semiconductor upside while converting industry volatility into distributions. He walks through four: (1) CHPY — YieldMax Semiconductor Portfolio Options Income ETF, holding 15-30 semiconductor names and using a call-spread strategy targeting ~40% annualized distribution with weekly payouts (range this year $0.38-$0.71/share). (2) SOXY — the YieldMax Target 12 semiconductor fund, a growth-leaning counterpart targeting 12% income so more upside stays in the portfolio (monthly payouts, $0.65 to over $1/share this year). (3) AMDY — a single-stock AMD options-income ETF for a tactical overweight on AMD, which he says he bought early last year and has since cashed. (4) NVDY — the single-stock Nvidia version targeting a 47% distribution rate. Suggested builds: max income = 70% CHPY / 15% NVDY / 15% AMDY; income-plus-growth = 50% SOXY / 25% AMDY / 25% NVDY. He flags the risks: distributions fluctuate with premiums and volatility, and income is never guaranteed. Calls made: CHPY BUY (~40% target), SOXY BUY (12% target), AMDY BUY, NVDY BUY (47% target). Other tickers discussed: MU (up ~1,200% over 5 years), MRVL (~+400%), NVDA (10x), ARM — all mentioned only as semiconductor theme leaders held inside the ETFs, not as direct calls. Note: captions rendered the second fund's ticker as 'SOX Y', with garbled repeats as 'SOXW' and 'SOXL' later in the video — the described product is consistently the Target 12 fund. _X0c2A-Ln9c.summary: Travis Hoeft (Asymmetric Investing) — 'Risk Warning: 5 Stocks to Sell Before It's Too Late' (published 29 Sep 2026). Core thesis: five of the market's most popular AI-related stocks are vastly overvalued, and their improved financials are a mirage because AI capex doesn't hit the income statement until assets are in use. The common thread is deteriorating credit: borrowing costs are rising both market-wide and company-specific, execution is stumbling, and debt markets could eventually close to these names. (1) ORCL SELL — Oracle is down 53% over the past year; trailing-12-month free cash flow is -$28B against nearly $120B of debt, the 10-year borrowing rate has risen from 5.7% in February to ~7.3%, and the Project Jupiter data center invoking force majeure is 'not normal' — a sign of real execution problems behind $664B of remaining performance obligations. (2) CRWV SELL — CoreWeave carries a $47B market cap on just $7.6B of trailing revenue, $35B of debt, and burned -$5.7B of free cash flow in Q2 2026 alone; its June 2026 8.5% notes now yield over 12%, ROIC is negative. (3) MU SELL — take profits on Micron ($1.2T market cap): the ~7x forward P/E looks cheap only if 83-86% gross margins hold, but memory is a commodity — capacity lands in 2028-29, chip designs are shifting away from expensive HBM, and margin reversion to 40% would wipe out ~90% of profits. (4) AMZN SELL — retail growth has slowed (~13% TTM) and its $39B of retail operating profit is essentially the advertising business, which is threatened by agentic AI shopping (Muse/ChatGPT buy without viewing ads); estimated -$34B free cash flow in 2026, 26x forward P/E. (5) TSLA SELL — revenue flat for three years, operating margins down to 2-4.2% (a regular automaker), trading at 13x sales / 192x forward earnings, with ~$26B of capex expected to exceed operating cash flow, while Musk's attention shifts to SpaceX. Notable: two days after Joseph Hogue rated ORCL and CRWV AVOID on this same watch, Hoeft escalates both to outright SELL. Captions render CoreWeave as 'Cororeweave' throughout — ticker CRWV confirmed against the company discussed.

sY9DIuxZzmc.title: Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock
sY9DIuxZzmc.creator: Daniel Pronk
sY9DIuxZzmc.summary: In 'Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock' (published 30 Sep 2026), Daniel Pronk returns from two weeks in Italy to reassure viewers asking whether Meta's ~30% rally from the lows has made it expensive. His answer: no — his DCF still shows a $827 fair value on conservative inputs (15% annual operating-cash-flow growth, 14x price/OCF) and ~$1,000 on realistic ones (20% growth, 15x OCF, still below the 16x historical median), implying 15-22.6% annualized returns over three years. The video's first half is a long showcase of Meta's new Muse AI agent: over 3 million US downloads in 9 days, #1 on the App Store for two weeks, adopted faster than ChatGPT, and Pronk's own daily use cases — sponsorship email triage, media kits, and home-purchase paperwork, all via email access. He argues Muse rides Meta's free distribution across Instagram and WhatsApp, and its clearest monetization is harvesting user data to sharpen ad targeting. He is skeptical of Zuckerberg's 'savings-shared' monetization model (Muse touches no transaction) and unconvinced agentic AI will fully disrupt Amazon/Booking.com advertising — window-shopping behavior persists. On Meta Connect: Muse at the center, the teased 'watermelon' frontier model, impressive new VR glasses, and a questionable Meta Charm pocket device. Call: META — BUY (adding), still undervalued at ~23x next year's earnings; he will add when post-house-closing liquidity frees up. No other tickers called.

989CUhoOUg8.title: Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]
989CUhoOUg8.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
989CUhoOUg8.summary: In 'Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]' (published 30 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA frames a Warren Buffett warning about part of the market 'going to hell' around the 10-year Treasury hitting a 24-year high. He attributes surging rates to four forces: persistent inflation (gas-driven CPI +3.4%), Uncle Sam's $2 trillion deficit, an AI-debt boom (Goldman sees hyperscaler debt issuance at a record $420B next year), and unexpectedly strong economic growth (flash PMI at a 5-year high) forcing the Fed toward more hikes. Five stocks to buy for this regime: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) — ~$360B in cash and T-bills collecting tens of billions at high rates, with financials/insurers in its portfolio earning more interest income; CME and CBOE — both down up to 17% last month on prediction-market competition fears, beneficiaries of rate-uncertainty hedging volume with a near-term bounce coming; the VanEck gold miners ETF (GDX) as a safety bet on inflation, deficits, and dollar weakness; and Vanguard's long-term bond ETF (BLV) — a conditional buy ("a little early"), attractive once rates level off, with a ~5% dividend and a possible bounce to $70 in the next recession. Six stocks to avoid: high-debt JBLU (debt/equity 591%, negative operating cash flow) and CCL (down 26% YTD, a falling knife), plus housing-chain DHI, PHM, BLDR, and Z as mortgage rates top 7%. Notable stance flip: Bank of America (BAC) moves from AVOID (Sep 28, long-term AI threat to financials) to BUY here — Hogue explicitly splits the time horizon: rate income now, AI disruption later. Sponsored Kalshi per-futures segment and a note that he is 'deeply invested in Ethereum' are mentions, not calls.

Ad2Pn32TWSs.title: Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!
Ad2Pn32TWSs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
Ad2Pn32TWSs.summary: In 'Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!' (published 1 Oct 2026, covering Micron's Sep 30 post-close print), Jose Najarro — who does not own the stock — argues the triple beat (revenue, EPS, and next-quarter guidance all well above consensus) leaves Micron cheap, with the flat after-hours reaction reflecting already-high hopes. His bull case: pricing is doing the heavy lifting (DRAM revenue +27% YoY, NAND +42%, on only mid-single-digit bit growth), and Micron expects a tight market through 2027-28 even with mid-20s industry bit-shipment growth; 35% of revenue through 2030 is covered by multi-year take-or-pay contracts, with $150B of remaining performance obligations (at minimum contract prices, so the real figure could be much higher) and $32B in customer cash deposits. HBM repricing begins at the start of calendar 2027, Q1 is the gross-margin floor, and buybacks unlock after December 9 (the CHIPS Act incentive 2-year anniversary) — he would not be surprised by a $50B repurchase authorization. Watch items: DRAM sequential price growth is decelerating (from ~60% to the high teens), consumer PC/phone units face double-digit declines in 2026, and capex is stepping up past $50B in 2027 (funded by contracted demand, he stresses). Caveat: auto-captions heavily garble the reported figures (e.g. '$54.2 billion in revenue', '$33 in one quarter' EPS, '$60 to 63 billion' guide) — treat all numbers here as approximate. Call: MU — BUY ('still dirt cheap'), with a rerating as the prize and supply-tight AI demand as the engine. Also bullish on the wider semiconductor/neocloud space as a memory bottleneck 'extends the cycle'.

WHzxbGZoTPQ.title: Unloved Chinese Stocks - Value, Buy for 2X?
WHzxbGZoTPQ.creator: Sven Carlin
WHzxbGZoTPQ.summary: Sven Carlin works through the ~20 largest holdings of the China internet ETF - unloved after 13 years with no performance - screening for value: low P/Es, high cash flows, profitability and growth. Tencent (P/E ~15, dividends, buybacks, double-digit growth) is "interesting" on his buy-the-bad-mood/sell-the-exuberance framework; he owns Prosus as his Tencent proxy. JD.com he owns outright - the investment/profitability cycle swings 50-70%, with very high cash flow per share, dividend, 3.7% buyback yield and a logistics moat. Kuaishou is his standout free bet: core business at P/E ~7 with 68% ownership of Kling AI (raised ~$3B, growing 200%). Baidu trades near book value of its cash with AI/robotaxi optionality; Trip.com at P/E 10 with ~RMB 14B cash looks interesting; Tencent Music is cheap and profitable. Alibaba is "too high now" on declining legacy cash flows; NetEase and Lenovo are fairly priced holds. He avoids KE Holdings (P/E 26, frozen transaction market), Bilibili, GDS and Kingsoft Cloud. Overall: buy big-cap Chinese internet on weakness for ~50% minimum over three years, hold via ETF or directly, size ~10-15% of a global value portfolio - and only for European investors; he explicitly warns US investors off due to sanction/illiquidity risk (VIE structure, Taiwan). Note: auto-captions garble several names (Meituan as "Mu1", Kling AI as "Cling AI", renminbi as "raimi/remimi") - treat P/E and cash figures as approximate.

F6ds1vqtOTY.title: A Once in a Lifetime Financial Reset is Coming. (Why Stocks Are Next)
F6ds1vqtOTY.creator: Tom Nash
F6ds1vqtOTY.summary: Tom Nash reframes the "market crash is coming" narrative: a crash is certain, but the wrong question is 'will it crash?' - the right ones are whether your portfolio is protected and set up to profit from it. He walks through historical playbooks (1973 oil embargo, 1990 Iraq war, 2022 Ukraine) showing crashes followed by multi-year recoveries, and the volatility stats that make staying invested work (54% of days, 75% of years, 95% of decades, 100% of 20-year periods positive). His system: 12-month emergency fund, kill expensive debt, max tax-advantaged accounts, zero leverage, then a portfolio stress test using beta (a 50/50 S&P/Palantir portfolio falls ~60% in a 30% S&P drop). Stock selection: a big S&P 500 core as the "undefeated cheat code", elite businesses run through a 125-point scorecard, max 10 positions, dollar-cost average and double down on the way down (he bought Palantir at $6-9 in 2022). Emotions are the portfolio killer: 24-hour cooldown rule, don't check daily, write a personal "constitution". No explicit stock calls - Palantir, Tesla and Nvidia appear only as high-beta stress-test examples; the actionable recommendation is SPY as the core holding. Ends with a pitch for his free "panic-proof guide" and the academy (patreon.com/theMASH).

HWGUIaBgdd4.title: [BUY HEAVY!] THIS ONE Stock Runs the Sports Economy
HWGUIaBgdd4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
HWGUIaBgdd4.summary: In '[BUY HEAVY!] THIS ONE Stock Runs the Sports Economy' (published 2 Oct 2026), Joseph Hogue follows up on his earlier Genius Sports video, arguing the market still prices GENI as a narrow sports-betting data vendor while it is becoming the critical infrastructure layer of the $100B+ sports economy. He lays out five pillars: sportsbooks (Genius supplies official real-time data, streaming and trading tech into a $111B global betting market); leagues and teams (NFL, Premier League, NCAA partnerships turn games into monetizable digital products; PWC sees team valuations accelerating); broadcasters and the advertising layer (live game data plus the fan-graph/moments engine won 174 new advertisers in Q2, incl. McDonald's, Airbnb and YouTube TV; the Legend acquisition adds 320M+ annual visits); and prediction markets, where Genius already partners with Kalshi and Polymarket as trusted arbiter (their combined volume rose ~5x in 7 months). These reinforce each other as a flywheel. On valuation he stays near-term conservative: $12/share from 2026E $1.02B revenue at his 5-year average 3.2x P/S, then argues ~$20/share (~270% upside from under $6) if 2027 sales reach ~$1.4B and the stock re-rates to 4x sales (2024 level). He flags the bear case honestly: rising league-rights renewal costs, competition from Sportradar, and that the flywheel must convert into sustained cash flow (guidance: 60% FCF conversion by 2028). Call: GENI BUY.

4e4bnSjMDsg.title: The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month
4e4bnSjMDsg.creator: Asymmetric Investing
4e4bnSjMDsg.summary: In 'The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month' (published 2 Oct 2026), Travis Hoeft reveals his October buy for the Asymmetric (ACE Metro) portfolio: Zillow (Z), which he is buying as a 10x-over-10-years compounder despite the stock being down 61% over the past year. His four-part checklist — revenue growth, margin expansion, multiple expansion, buybacks — is, he argues, all present. Revenue is growing 17.7% and accelerating even in a weak housing market, driven by rentals ($734M TTM, +34% CAGR) and the mortgage leg rather than the traditional 8%-growth residential business; the company now positions itself as where people answer all housing questions, an aggregator that owns customer demand. Operating margin flipped from -13.5% (Mar-2024 quarter) to slightly positive, with $258M TTM free cash flow and ~$800M of recent buybacks shrinking shares from ~242M. Valuation looks unloved: ~11x forward P/E, ~15x forward P/FCF, 2.2x sales. His main criticism is stock-based compensation (still $363M, down from $423M) and he admits the housing market could get worse short-term, but sees that as the launching pad. Note: this is a cross-creator divergence — Joseph Hogue had Z as AVOID on 30 Sep on housing-supply-chain weakness. Call: Z BUY.

jAtRNbIWaOw.title: NVIDIA Just Changed the AI Market AGAIN — Here's What Comes Next
jAtRNbIWaOw.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
jAtRNbIWaOw.summary: In 'NVIDIA Just Changed the AI Market AGAIN — Here's What Comes Next' (published 4 Oct 2026), Jose Najarro walks through a week of Nvidia news he calls one 'oh snap' and several bullish moments. The 'oh snap': Nvidia's 1 Oct blog showing GPT-6 Astra running on Blackwell at up to 18x faster token generation undercuts the speed-moat story of Cerebras (CBRS, +~20% in five days pre-news), whose OpenAI ultra-fast partnership now looks exposed — though he says it is too early to call it game over and notes Altman's reassuring partnership comments as mildly bullish for Cerebras. Bullish for Nvidia: stock ~$238 (all-time high, ~$5.7T market cap, +23% YTD), OpenAI's Dots agentic AI driving more token consumption (he sees the supply/demand imbalance lasting through ~Oct 2028), and AWS raising GPU prices ~15% from 2 Oct (B300/B200, H100/H200, A100) as evidence demand still outstrips supply. He also reinforces his 1 Oct post-earnings MU BUY: the new 64GB DGX Spark at ~$5,000 (half the memory of the $4,000 128GB original, now $7,000) shows memory pricing is 'insane' and the shortage persists; Pixel 10a's $100 price hike is memory-driven too. Other names: neoclouds and hyperscalers broadly bullish, no specific calls; Cerebras discussed at length but no call (captions garble it as Cerebrus/soas/surreal shareholder). Calls: NVDA BUY (bullish continuation), MU BUY (thesis reinforced).

951xEYynOGo.title: The AI Stock Investors Just Got Another MASSIVE Bull Signal!!
951xEYynOGo.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
951xEYynOGo.summary: Jose Najarro covers Marvell Technology's investor day and Lisa Su's comments from Taipei, arguing both are fresh confirmation of the AI semiconductor demand cycle. Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20 billion (from $18 billion two months earlier, and $16.5 billion before that), with both raises driven by networking -- scale-up/scale-out optics and switching. Custom silicon's FY2029 target is now over $12 billion versus $10 billion-plus reaffirmed in August, and the FY2031 model calls for $70-90 billion in revenue implying over $30 of non-GAAP EPS at the midpoint. On simple math he sketches a $600 potential stock price (30x on $30 CY2030 EPS), stressing it is 4-5 years out and that he would not claim it as a base case. He treats the day as bullish confirmation for his 'ETF approach' trio of Marvell, Credo Technology (dip into the $150s-$160s was a buy, he says; up ~4%) and Astera Labs (up ~8%), and reads Broadcom as the bigger beneficiary given it leads the semi-custom market Marvell is chasing. Su's Taiwan remarks on expanding CPU/GPU production and wafer capacity are framed as another 'brick' in his bullish thesis house, with server CPU revenue guided up over 70% in 2027 and data-center revenue expected to more than double; he notes the server CPU market estimate grew from $60 billion (Nov 2025) to $220 billion. Calls: MRVL BUY (~$600 potential CY2030 model), AMD BUY, AVGO BUY (read-through), CRDO BUY ($150s-$160s dip zone), ALAB BUY. NVDA and MU mentioned only in passing. Caption notes: auto-captions garble Marvell as 'Marll'/'Marvel', Broadcom as 'Broncom', Credo as 'Credto', and Lisa Su as 'Lisa Sue'.

czgmVfoNao4.title: 5 Stocks to Buy BEFORE the 2027 AI Bank Crash
czgmVfoNao4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
czgmVfoNao4.summary: Joseph Hogue argues AI agents (spurred by Meta's Muse launch, ~3M downloads by late September) will remove the friction that keeps tens of millions of customers in legacy banks paying 0.01-0.04% on deposits, forcing traditional banks into a damned-if-you-do choice: lose deposits or match ~3.5% rates and crater net interest income. His back-of-envelope stress test puts the industry hit at up to $52B, with JPMorgan (a $900B market cap bank paying 0.01%) risking ~$30B of its $95B interest income and Citigroup ~$5.5B. He ranks five legacy banks as avoids - Citigroup, JPMorgan, U.S. Bancorp, Wells Fargo and Bank of America - though he names Bank of America (1.37x book, 0.71x PEG, 8.5% expected revenue growth) the best relative deal of the group if buying the selloff. His five buys are the fintech beneficiaries: SoFi (32% expected revenue growth, 0.69x PEG, "a great deal"), Coinbase (3.5% USDC rewards, tokenization tailwind), Robinhood (31% growth, 2.4x PEG), PayPal (1.4x PEG, slower 4.4% growth but cheap) and Ally Financial (0.85x book, 0.3x PEG, the value pick). He is transparent that the stress test is crude - banks could respond with fees or funding shifts - and that the shift plays out over years, not weeks. Calls: SOFI/COIN/HOOD/PYPL/ALLY BUY (PYPL and ALLY reiterations); C/JPM/USB/WFC/BAC AVOID - BAC is a stance flip from his Oct 1 BUY. The video includes a sponsored Monarch money-app segment.

1Js-3kgdOMw.title: 3 Positive Asymmetric Buys From The Bets Quadrant...
1Js-3kgdOMw.creator: Sven Carlin
1Js-3kgdOMw.summary: Sven Carlin updates the "bets" side of his value-investing quadrant with three positive asymmetric risk/reward ideas, stressing these are bets, not margin-of-safety value investments. On Lululemon he details Michael Burry's tax-loss harvest (bought ~$200, sold everything at a ~50% loss after a one-day rotation into Deckers, likely back in January after the 30-day wash rule) and argues nothing happens for 45-60 days: wait ~3 months, watch for year-end tax-loss selling and the new CEO's likely kitchen-sink first call. His three bets: Kuaishou (P/E 7, 400M daily users, Kling AI IPO next year with Hogue's 68% stake worth ~HKD 12B against a legacy business valued near HKD 4B), Pinduoduo ($107B market cap, $66B cash -> ~4x P/E ex-cash, investing RMB 100B to build a third business), and Charter Communications (~3x free cash flow on an adjusted $16B market cap, a 2x if rates turn but saddled with $120B of refinancing risk). He explicitly rejects Uber ("no Uber for me" - no moat, acquisition-fueled growth), Adobe (slow AI-driven decline), Google ("no way Jose"), Birkenstock (quality deterioration anecdote plus PE ownership change), and Petrobras drilling (squeeze bet he no longer takes). Tencent Music moves from the bets quadrant to his investment quadrant. He walks through Mohnish Pabrai's concentrated bucket bets (Transocean/Valaris rigs, Mark Leonard/Constellation, Turkey, coal, India financials) as idea sources he is mostly too uncomfortable to take, and notes Alibaba only gets interesting below $100 (sold his last at $175). Calls: KUAIS/PDD/CHTR CONDITIONAL_BUY (KUAIS softened from Oct 2 BUY; PDD upgraded from UNCERTAIN); BIRK/UBER/GOOGL/ADBE/PBR AVOID; LULU/BABA UNCERTAIN; KSPI HOLD (owned). Auto-captions garble names (Pabrai as "Pabry", Kling as "Cling", Kuaishou as "Quao").

vFGkr80KPBw.title: ONE Stock is All You Need in This $5 Trillion Opportunity
vFGkr80KPBw.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
vFGkr80KPBw.summary: Hogue frames humanoid robotics as the "$5 trillion opportunity" (Morgan Stanley's estimate of a ~930M-humanoid market by 2050) and pitches Robo Strategy (BOT), a Nasdaq-listed closed-end fund, as the single vehicle giving everyday investors pre-IPO access to private robotics leaders - Figure, Apptronik, Dyna Robotics and Standard Bots - they would otherwise never reach. He walks through the closed-end mechanics investors must understand: the difference between the fund's NAV ($11.35/share as of Aug 31, ~$277M net assets) and its market price, with an illustrative $25 vs $11.35 NAV example showing a 2x+ premium. He warns speculation fatigue and a liquidity need could hit the price, while conceding the market cap is still small enough that speculation could carry it to $500,000 or $1,000,000. gLwAhfTnJfE.title: The UNTHINKABLE is About to Happen to the Stock Market (& Why AI Stocks are Next)
gLwAhfTnJfE.creator: Tom Nash
gLwAhfTnJfE.summary: Tom Nash argues the recent fear-driven selloff — a hot inflation print on Wednesday, the S&P 500 down about 1.1% and ending a six-year streak without a 1% down day, Nasdaq and small caps down about 2% — exposes lack of conviction rather than broken companies. His core claim is that a stock rising 1,000% does not make most holders money: using Palantir's path from $10 to $40, down to $6 for a year, then to about $200, he says most retail investors buy hype and sell bottoms. The fix, in his system, is research, consistency, a system and conviction, built slowly like fitness or learning an instrument. He recaps his Roic Academy top-stocks list — Nvidia up almost 1,500% since October 2020, Palantir up about 1,900%, plus ANET, ASML, Micron, AMD, ARM, Datadog and Bloom Energy — stressing each suffered 20–75% drawdowns on the way. He gives seven checks for a falling stock: revenue growth, expanding margins, lost contracts or clients, rising debt, key executive departures, weak forecasts and new competitors. His worked example is Zeta Global, pitched in May 2026 after a 50% fall since November 2024 and up 92% since, on 30% revenue growth to $1.3 billion, free cash flow up 100% and more cash than debt. His rules: never time the market, double down when the S&P is 10% below its 52-week high or a single name is 20% below, trim at +50/+100/+150%, and check the portfolio at most weekly. The video mainly funnels to a free masterclass on Saturday 24 October at 2pm Eastern, promising his research-system document and a never-before-mentioned bullish pick. No new individual stock calls are made; tickers named are historical examples and system illustrations only.

IaSD9j5O_ZQ.title: $160K Down in ONE DAY! Why I'm BUYING These 15 Stocks
IaSD9j5O_ZQ.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA

He plans to roughly double his 1,500-share Alibaba (BABA) position at $109 before early-November earnings, betting its Qwen open-source model wins as token volumes explode, and he is still holding Symbotic (SYM). In cybersecurity — his favourite long-term theme — he is picking up more Zscaler (ZS), pauses on Fortinet (FTNT) and Okta (OKTA), and holds CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto (PANW). He also endorses SoFi (SOFI) back in at $15.89, holds SoundHound (SOUN) and Grab (GRAB), and trails a Wednesday video on rotating from AI hardware into application names such as SoundHound, Cloudflare, ServiceNow, Snowflake and Salesforce. Calls: ETHA HOLD, SMCI SELL, BABA BUY, SYM HOLD, CRWD HOLD, PANW HOLD, FTNT HOLD, OKTA HOLD, ZS BUY, SOFI BUY, SOUN HOLD, GRAB HOLD, NOW UNCERTAIN. Captions garble several items — Alibaba's model as 'Qin', Mastercard's payments network as 'global patent payments network', and Ethereum price history — tickers and stances above are the companies actually discussed.

fOe_Ck6pBsE.title: 10 AI Stocks Down as Much as 25% — Is the Market Wrong?
fOe_Ck6pBsE.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
fOe_Ck6pBsE.summary: Jose Najarro works through 10 AI stocks across five parts of the AI build-out after a 9-16 October sell-off he attributes mainly to AI financing fears centred on CoreWeave's debt, arguing the long-term AI story is still early and TSMC/ASML commentary confirms demand for years. In neoclouds he is very bullish on CoreWeave (CRWV) — $105bn-plus backlog, 1.5 GW, enterprise expansion — and gives Nebius (NBIS) a positive but non-committal review, noting he does not own it. In memory, Micron (MU) is a new, small portfolio position on locked-in customer agreements and HBM pricing, and he likes FormFactor (FORM) at ~$105 and plans to buy back in. In optics he covers Lumentum (LITE), which he does not own, and Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI). In AI chips he covers Marvell (MRVL) and Cerebras (CBRS) cautiously on valuation and competition. Networking is a favourite area: Credo (CRDO) is a top pick at a ~25.5x forward P/E, and Astera Labs (ALAB) is a held, bullish name despite a ~66x near-term multiple. He discloses he bought stocks in the sell-off and does not own NBIS, FORM or LITE. Calls: CRWV BUY, NBIS UNCERTAIN, MU BUY, FORM BUY, LITE UNCERTAIN, AAOI BUY, MRVL BUY, CBRS UNCERTAIN, CRDO BUY, ALAB BUY. Captions garble names throughout — Nebius as 'Nebulae', Lumentum as 'Lights', Cerebras as 'Coriant'/'So Reapers' — and several figures (Micron revenue, AAOI unit capacity, Lumentum's ~$820 price) are caption-uncertain; Soitec was named in the opening list of 10 but got no dedicated section.

v5NMsQnpR2Q.title: NVIDIA Stock: Meta Just Confirmed the AI Demand Is REAL!!
v5NMsQnpR2Q.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
v5NMsQnpR2Q.summary: Jose Najarro examines Meta's Prometheus AI supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, arguing it confirms real AI demand. The first phase is complete with hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GPUs training Meta's Muse models, with a future target of roughly one million distributed GPUs working in lockstep across sites because power limits prevent a single site holding them all. He contrasts GB200 and GB300 racks — the GB300 moves to a single-rack layout at about 135 kW, with Vera Rubin above 170 kW and fully liquid-cooled trays — and argues simpler layouts help cooling, cost and reliability. Reliability is a central theme: interruptions per 8,000 GPUs per day were very high for GB200 in mid-2025, are much lower for GB300, and Meta targets about two, with 64 active plus eight spare GPUs in each 72-GPU domain and goodput above 85% for Muse pre-training and above 90% for reinforcement learning. He also covers power capping, batteries and liquid cooling, and the backend aggregation network, where Arista 7800 switches use Broadcom Jericho. Nvidia is called the big winner; Broadcom and Arista are named networking beneficiaries, and a brief garbled caption reference appears to mention Marvell among networking names he likes. Calls: NVDA BUY (reiterated, no price stated); META, AVGO and ANET UNCERTAIN — positive/beneficiary coverage with no explicit buy or hold stated in this video. Captions garble several names, including Muse/Watermelon and GB200/GB300 renderings.

OZBaYC2tTDk.title: Netflix Stock Is Crashing - What You Need To Know
OZBaYC2tTDk.creator: Daniel Pronk
OZBaYC2tTDk.summary: Daniel Pronk reviews Netflix's Q3 report after the stock fell almost 6% in after-hours, on top of being down almost 50% from its all-time high. Revenue rose 12% year-on-year (11% FX-neutral, in line) and operating margin beat at 34.6%, but full-year 2026 revenue guidance was trimmed from $51.2B to $51.1B and the Q4 advertising revenue guide was cut 10% (about $300M) — the key disappointment, since advertising is meant to be the next growth and margin driver. He stresses continued revenue deceleration (about 18% to an 11.5% Q4 guide) across regions, weak watch time (India, its showcase market, grew hours 24% but only low-to-mid single digits per member), and US TV share losses to YouTube. US growth looks largely price-led after two rises in just over a year. Cash flow is strong ($3.162B operating cash flow in Q3), though flattered by a one-time Warner Bros breakup fee, and buybacks ($4.8B in Q3, $10.8B year-to-date) exceeded free cash flow, funded by about $1B of new debt. At roughly 22x trailing and 20x forward normalised earnings the stock only interests him if the moat holds and earnings compound 10–15%; he is more sceptical than confident, does not own it, and would not buy here. Call: NFLX — AVOID, no share price stated. No other tickers are given calls; Amazon and Google appear only as competitors.

0UT-qmch2jU.title: Why AI Stocks Are Falling (It’s Worse Than You Think)
0UT-qmch2jU.creator: Asymmetric Investing
0UT-qmch2jU.summary: Travis Hoium (Asymmetric Investing) argues the AI sell-off is a financing reckoning centred on the neoclouds — CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren, with Oracle grouped in. Over five days to Friday's recording Oracle fell about 9%, Nebius about 19%, and Iren and CoreWeave about 22%. His three drivers: first, Anthropic's revenue growth has stalled month-on-month (about +1.8% over four weeks, after +46% quarter-on-quarter in Q3), while the capex already committed needs AI revenue to reach about $3 trillion by 2031 — Dylan Patel's framing, quoted in the video, is that OpenAI and Anthropic alone must reach hundreds of billions by end-2027 or 'we're in real trouble'. Second, buyers are capping AI spend (Accenture's $29-a-month Claude limit; Uber, Meta and Microsoft ending unlimited 'token maxing'), so willingness to pay, not token demand, is the question. Third, CoreWeave's 9% February 2031 debt yield has risen from about 8% in May to over 15%, implying a 20–25% equity hurdle that makes new data centres unprofitable — a doom loop for names that must keep raising capital, while cash-generative hyperscalers can pause. He is not in this part of the trade and expects more collapses. Calls: CRWV, NBIS, IREN and ORCL — AVOID (CRWV and ORCL were SELL on his 29 Sep sell list, so this is a stance change in form, with the bearish thesis unchanged); GOOGL — HOLD (owned, 'going to be just fine', no price stated). Caption figures for Patel's revenue projections are garbled in places.

3h3vRJnRLbE.title: NVIDIA Stock Investors... Elon Musk Just Delivered HUGE News!!
3h3vRJnRLbE.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
3h3vRJnRLbE.summary: Jose Najarro treats Elon Musk's SpaceXAI/xAI earnings commentary (auto-captions render the company as 'SpaceX' throughout, and Nebius as 'Debbie') and a Super Micro pre-announcement as a bullish win for AI and semiconductor investors. Super Micro raised fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5B — about a $4B, or 26.7%, increase — and gross margin guidance to 12–12.5% from 10.4–10.8%, which he reads as huge server demand with pricing power ahead of full results on 3 November. On xAI he cites about 1.7 GW of active compute at 30 September, roughly 2 GW by end-October and 2.5 GW by year-end, about 13 GW targeted by the end of next year, roughly 200,000 Nvidia GB300s coming online per month, a $500B–$1T ARR projection for end-2027, roughly $40B of Q4 capex, and sub-one-year (potentially six-month) payback on new compute. His read-through: if xAI spends at that pace, hyperscaler capex guidance above $300B next year is plausible, so he stays bullish and calm on the industry. Calls: NVDA — BUY reiterated, no price stated (up about 2% on the day); SMCI — UNCERTAIN (bullish coverage, no explicit buy stated); META — UNCERTAIN (expects a bullish earnings report tomorrow in the video's timeframe, no explicit buy stated). CoreWeave, Nebius, Iren, Amazon, AMD, Intel and Micron appear only in a green-day price roundup, with no calls.

VpIy9dfKK9I.title: Meta Stock Is Up After Earnings - What You Need To Know
VpIy9dfKK9I.creator: Daniel Pronk
VpIy9dfKK9I.summary: Daniel Pronk reviews Meta's Q3 earnings as a shareholder, calling the report messy but ultimately good. Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.6 billion and daily active people reached 3.64 billion, with ad impressions up 10% and average ad price up 14%. Costs were hit by a pre-announced $9.89 billion legal charge, which suppressed operating income, although net income rose sharply on the comparison in the captions. Capex was $34.91 billion against $32.8 billion of operating cash flow, making Meta free-cash-flow negative for the quarter, and Pronk expects negative free cash flow into 2027, more debt, and some dilution after Meta created a new Class C share for capital raising and stock compensation. He stresses the positives: headcount down 15% while revenue grows, average revenue per person at an all-time high of $17.72, Q4 revenue guidance around $74.5 billion at the midpoint, and Muse passing 10 million downloads with shopping as its main use case. His updated DCF, using 15% operating-cash-flow growth and a 14-times multiple, implies about 17% annual compounding. Call: META — HOLD, continuing to hold and looking to increase the position if shares fall; no current share price was stated, and several percentage figures are missing or garbled in the auto-captions.

gYOUhwmQqs4.title: 7 Stocks to Buy When the AI Bubble Turns 2000
gYOUhwmQqs4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
gYOUhwmQqs4.summary: Joseph Hogue argues the AI sell-off in CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle echoes the dot-com bust: the whole buildout rests on OpenAI and Anthropic revenue that public investors cannot yet audit, and he expects the real break three to six months after Anthropic's IPO, when several quarters of results are visible. Like Amazon after 2000, he says the winners will be companies using AI rather than building infrastructure, and he is buying seven of them slowly — a little now, more every month or two, while holding cash back for a crash. The seven are UiPath, ServiceNow, Palantir, Cloudflare, SoundHound AI, Tempus AI (captions say 'Tempest AI') and Snowflake, each assessed on operating and free cash flow, balance-sheet cash and survivability if financing dries up, with analyst targets shown for context. Palantir is the exception on timing: he wants $150–$160 before loading up. DwQ8z2cn7H0.title: NVIDIA Just Changed AI Data Centers FOREVER!!
DwQ8z2cn7H0.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
DwQ8z2cn7H0.summary: Jose Najarro covers Nvidia's GTC Berlin announcements and earnings from Lam Research, Texas Instruments and Meta. The headline is Nvidia's DSX pods: shipping containers pre-built with Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, power and cooling, which he says cut AI-factory build time from about six months to as little as 14 days, reducing lender and execution risk and reinforcing Nvidia as the only supplier offering this. On Lam Research (captions say 'Lamb Research'), down about 7.4% after a narrow beat, he says he is not a shareholder but would not fear the sell-off, noting wafer-fab equipment spending above $200 billion expected in 2027. On Texas Instruments, Q3 revenue was $6.06 billion, up 28% year over year, with data-centre revenue up about 95%, industrial up over 40% and automotive up mid-teens. On Meta, he calls the report extremely bullish for the AI cycle: revenue up 26%, Q4 guidance of $73–76 billion, the capex lower bound raised to $135 billion, strong Muse adoption, and a new Class C share he reads as preparation for large capex fundraising. Calls: NVDA — BUY reiterated, very bullish, no price stated; LRCX — UNCERTAIN (first tracked, positive coverage only); TXN — UNCERTAIN (first tracked, positive coverage only); META — UNCERTAIN (bullish read-through only, no explicit buy).

HK0hFkXskQc.title: Dying Business or Generational Opportunity? FICO's drop explained.
HK0hFkXskQc.creator: Brian Feroldi
HK0hFkXskQc.summary: Brian Feroldi asks whether Fair Isaac (FICO) is a dying business or a generational opportunity after a fall of about 66% from its all-time high. He explains FICO's two segments: credit scores, about two-thirds of revenue, and bank software for account opening, fraud and marketing, about one-third. Revenue was about $2.4 billion over the last 12 months, roughly 90% from the Americas, with over $1 billion of operating cash flow and no dividend — a phase-four, capital-return business. He calls the moat wide: software lock-in, the FICO score as a de facto regulatory standard, a very strong brand and 54% returns on capital. Growth has not collapsed: revenue rose more than 20% and earnings 25% over the last year, analysts expect about 28% revenue growth in 2027, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance. He gives three reasons for the fall. First, aggressive mortgage-score pricing — from about 60 cents to $10 since 2022 — angered lenders, drew monopoly criticism and pushed Rocket Mortgage toward VantageScore. Second, a September 2026 move by the FHFA's Bill Pulte put FICO and VantageScore on one pricing grid, removing FICO's government preference; VantageScore is offered at 99 cents. Third, FICO borrowed heavily for $2.3 billion of buybacks, likely above 30 times earnings. At about 23 times earnings versus a 10-year average near 50 times, Feroldi leans opportunity over trap, but says the damaged moat means he wants an even cheaper valuation before getting excited. Call: FICO — CONDITIONAL_BUY, first tracked, no dollar price stated.

dR8CQ1FJzyQ.title: Stock Market Crash: What to Watch Next
dR8CQ1FJzyQ.creator: Asymmetric Investing
dR8CQ1FJzyQ.summary: Travis Hoium (Asymmetric Investing) explains a big down day for AI names — technology, software and semiconductors were broadly red, with stalwarts such as Apple and Walmart among the few gainers — and argues the move is investors questioning the return on another trillion dollars of AI spending. About 50% of the S&P 500 is now tied to the AI trade, from memory and energy to chips and hyperscalers, so any slowdown in spending growth could hit the whole market. His indicators are financing costs: CoreWeave's 9% 2031 debt trades at a 14.6% yield, Nebius's September convertible trades at about 85 cents on the dollar and below its convert price, and credit-default swaps have risen for hyperscalers, led by Oracle and including Alphabet, AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Amazon and SpaceX. Meta, Alphabet and Amazon have crossed into negative free cash flow, so even hyperscalers must raise capital, though they can pull back capex; neoclouds cannot, and CoreWeave's expected capex dwarfs its $5.5 billion cash. He cites Anthropic's slowed growth and IBM, Uber, Microsoft and Accenture curbing AI spend as ROI canaries, warns chip sellers such as Nvidia, AMD, Micron and TSMC face revenue, margin and multiple contraction if growth slows, and notes his portfolio was up nearly 1% on the day because he owns durable, cash-generative names — Alphabet is his only core AI holding. Calls: CRWV — AVOID, NBIS — AVOID, GOOGL — HOLD (all reiterated, no prices stated). Caption names are garbled in places (CoreWeave, Nebius).

ZEImdkhIF6g.title: 🚨MAJOR BUY: Last EASY Wealth Opportunity For Decades
ZEImdkhIF6g.creator: Tom Nash
ZEImdkhIF6g.summary: Tom Nash argues the recent sell-off (Nasdaq down over 5% in 30 days, S&P 500 down 1.6%, Nvidia down 6.3%) is fear, not a thesis break, and presents it as a major buying opportunity. He reviews his 18 December 2025 top-15 list: 11 of 15 rose, for a 28.5% average return versus 12.5% for the S&P 500, and his May second-wave list, where six of seven rose for a 32.5% average versus 0.5% for the index. His anti-bubble case has four parts: forward P/E on the S&P 500 is 19, the 10-year average, while earnings grow about 29.5%; expensive money restrains euphoria; the fear-and-greed index is at extreme fear (21); and there is no IPO or meme mania, with tight credit and high volatility showing no complacency. He says AI will move from infrastructure (wave one: Nvidia, AMD, TSMC, Vertiv) to implementation, where the larger returns sit. Only two of his new top 11 are named in the video - ARM and AppLovin; the other nine are only in a free downloadable report. Calls: ARM - BUY (down ~50%, revenue +22%, $4bn cash, zero debt) and APP - BUY (down ~65%, ~50% growth, $4.5bn free cash flow), both first tracked for Nash.

S3pQiAXNVPU.title: BUY HEAVY! If You Miss These 4 Stocks, You’ll Regret it in 5 Days

ServiceNow reports Wednesday with a pulled-forward federal contract to overcome, and Amazon reports Thursday as his free-cash-flow warning case after $220bn capex guidance. Reddit reports Thursday with Google licensing and Anthropic lawsuit catalysts, and he updates Netflix after last week's disappointment, disclosing a 4,000-share position at $65. WCBrbbiIGKA.title: NVIDIA Stock Is Crashing...But AI Demand Is NOT Slowing Down!!
WCBrbbiIGKA.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
WCBrbbiIGKA.summary: Jose Najarro examines why AI stocks have fallen for two to three weeks - the Nasdaq fell about 2.6% on 22 October, Nvidia about 4%, Meta about 7% after earnings and Lam Research about 12%, with neoclouds also down - and argues the market is questioning financing and payback timing, not whether AI demand exists. He separates timing risk, overbuild risk and financing cost, citing SemiAnalysis figures for more than 24 GW in advanced construction across 40 campuses and potentially about 50 GW turning on in 2027. Nvidia is his central example: DSX pods cut deployment from six months to as little as 14 days, a third-party financing platform targets over $500 billion of capital over time, and revenue backstops support selected projects, though Nvidia is not itself the lender. He works through Meta (revenue $64.6 billion, free cash flow about -$2 billion in the quarter, Muse demand), SpaceX/xAI (captions render it SpaceX; rapid compute growth, sub-one-year payback claims, and Elon Musk's weekend warnings about stranded compute and neocloud financing), Nebius's $3.5 billion Citi facility as evidence financing remains selective, CoreWeave's active power base, and Lam Research upstream. Calls: NVDA - BUY (reiterated), META - UNCERTAIN and LRCX - UNCERTAIN (both positive coverage only, reiterated). Caption renderings are garbled in places, notably Lam Research as 'Lamb' and Nebius variants.

lbF1dMRllI4.title: Anthopic's S1 Just Saved The AI Trade - What You Need To Know
lbF1dMRllI4.creator: Daniel Pronk
lbF1dMRllI4.summary: Daniel Pronk walks through Anthropic's newly released S-1 filing and argues it has reversed the recent AI sell-off, with AI names spiking again while hyperscalers sell off. He traces revenue from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024, $4.6 billion in 2025 and $16.3 billion year to date in 2026, calling the growth unprecedented, and stresses the headline $80.7 billion net loss is dominated by a $72.4 billion non-cash fair-value loss on convertible shares. On his reading the business is near break-even operationally: adjusted operating margin reached 19% in Q2, operating cash flow was positive $3.9 billion year to date, free cash flow was $3.5 billion on a GAAP basis, and the balance sheet holds $112.4 billion of cash plus $19.3 billion of short-term investments against only $7.2 billion of current liabilities. Consumption-based revenue is 80% of the total, customers over $100,000 of annual spend rose 8x year over year to 11,900, and compute efficiency improved 5.2x. He cites customer examples including AIG, Bristol Myers, DoorDash and Mercado Libre, plus his own use of Muse for his channel. Against that he flags a mooted $1.5 to 2 trillion IPO valuation at 30 to 40 times annualised revenue and roughly $800 billion of future spending commitments. Calls: none recorded — he explicitly says he is not looking to invest in Anthropic or buy its IPO, and Anthropic has no public ticker yet; Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Broadcom appear only as commitment counterparties, with no direction stated for them. Captions garble Anthropic as 'Anthopic' in the title.

Qf72K1Fends.title: AI Chip Shortages Could Last Until 2030...This Changes Everything
Qf72K1Fends.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
Qf72K1Fends.summary: Jose Najarro argues AI chip shortages could last to 2030 and that this extends, rather than ends, the AI cycle. The anchor is SK Hynix earnings: HBM volume requirements more than twice current supply, DRAM and HBM through 2026 effectively sold out, lower-stack concerns already reflected in shipment plans, HBM4 yield above plan, and long-term agreements allocating more than 50 percent of 2027 and 2028 capacity, giving capex visibility that he calls bullish for equipment players too. He then works through Galaxy and CoreWeave (79 million dollars of Q3 data-center adjusted gross profit, Helios phase 1 delivered, phase 2 fully financed), Meta partnerships with AMD (Helios MI450 systems installed, a 1 billion dollar equity figure as captioned) and Nvidia (expanded Vera Rubin work, a 3 billion dollar figure as captioned), a report that OpenAI may buy Google TPUs, which he does not read as bearish for Nvidia in a compute-starved market, and Oracle broadening its stack ahead of its investor day. He concludes his bullish thesis is unchanged ahead of Alphabet and Microsoft earnings. Calls: NVDA and AMD and CRWV BUY reiterated, META and AVGO and CBRS UNCERTAIN reiterated, SK Hynix (000660.KS) and GOOGL and ORCL UNCERTAIN first tracked. No prices stated. Captions garble SK Hynix, Helios and CoreWeave throughout.

OTjsHhkHXEY.title: The Market Hated Google's Earnings - Here's Why
OTjsHhkHXEY.creator: Daniel Pronk
OTjsHhkHXEY.summary: Daniel Pronk works through Alphabet's Q3 2026 earnings after an 11 percent after-hours drop, building his own read before checking the market's reaction. Revenue rose 25 percent year over year to 127.6 billion dollars, with Google Cloud up 103 percent — now including TPU sales — and Gemini at 1 billion users, but the core businesses decelerated to 11 percent growth, with search at 12 percent, YouTube ads at 9 percent and subscriptions at 11 percent. He argues the headline net income and EPS declines are meaningless because of unrealised investment gains, and that operating income (up 30 percent, 32 percent margin) is the cleanest valuation metric. The negatives he expects the market to punish are the operating cash flow decline, negative free cash flow of 9 billion dollars in the quarter on 51.3 billion dollars of capex, share dilution after 42 billion dollars raised this year, and conference-call guidance of margin pressure, higher 2027 capex and AI Mode monetising below search. His verdict is that Google is now fairly valued at about 24.5 times operating income, back to its decade median, with the premium gone — but he is not adding here, preferring to keep buying Meta and Amazon, which he believes offer more value. Other tickers discussed are Meta and Amazon, the latter's earnings video promised for the next day.

HooqeUxWhOk.title: Google's 7% Drop: Should You Sell or Hold? | $GOOG $GOOGL
HooqeUxWhOk.creator: Asymmetric Investing
HooqeUxWhOk.summary: Travis Williams of Asymmetric Investing gives an initial reaction to Alphabet's Q3 earnings, recorded before the conference call, answering the title question with a hold: Alphabet is not a stock he is going to be selling anytime soon. He argues the earnings miss is widely misunderstood — a one-time 8.7 billion dollar mark-to-market loss on equity positions in SpaceX and Anthropic cut reported EPS to 2.12 dollars versus about 3 dollars expected, while the adjusted figure is about 2.67 dollars. Beneath that, revenue grew 25 percent, operating income 30 percent, Cloud revenue 103 percent to 30.7 billion dollars at a 36.2 percent margin, and search grew 12 percent, faster than YouTube, with segment margins expanding more than two points — evidence, to him, that search is still monetising well despite disruption fears. He also notes general and administrative costs cut by over 1 billion dollars against heavy R&D spending, two straight quarters of negative free cash flow on 51 billion dollars of quarterly capex, and a balance sheet holding 265 billion dollars of cash against 125 billion dollars of debt. At about 22 times forward earnings the stock is not the cheapest, but he calls the report reasonably good, holds a position up about 100 percent, and promises a fuller follow-up later in the week.

STKzuRoEQoE.title: The AI Stock Market Just Got 3 Massive Signals!!

STKzuRoEQoE.summary: Jose Najarro covers three earnings and investor-day signals for AI and semiconductor investors: Alphabet, Microsoft and Oracle. On Alphabet, Cloud crossed 30 billion dollars for the first time, up 103 percent year over year with a 36.2 percent operating margin and TPU systems contributing meaningfully, making Google the fastest-growing hyperscaler; but search growth of 12 percent is the bearish flag, with AI Overviews cannibalising search faster than expected and monetising below traditional search, plus a second straight free-cash-flow-negative quarter of about 9.1 billion dollars. On Microsoft, Azure re-accelerated to 48 percent growth with 49 to 50 percent constant-currency guidance, beating roughly 44 percent expectations despite third-party GPU delays, and Microsoft stands out as the only free-cash-flow-positive hyperscaler at about 18 billion dollars, with calendar 2027 capex possibly reaching 225 to 250 billion dollars. On Oracle, fiscal 2027 revenue is targeted at 90 billion dollars and fiscal 2030 at over 225 billion dollars with over 21 dollars of EPS, implying north of 500 dollars at a 25 times multiple — though Oracle's statement that capex peaks in fiscal 2027-2028 then steps down in 2029, without sizing either, feeds fears of slower chip orders, which he argues is not the full picture since capex dollars do not equal chip units. No explicit buy or sell is stated for any of the three names.

ln-7LUU_9oE.title: Booking NASDAQ: BKNG Looks Like A Great Business Trading Cheap
ln-7LUU_9oE.creator: Sven Carlin
ln-7LUU_9oE.summary: Sven Carlin asks whether Booking Holdings (BKNG) is a great business trading cheap after falling about 24% since its August high (28% at one point in the video). On fundamentals he is enthusiastic: trailing-12-month revenue and net income both up 8%, diluted earnings per share up 15% thanks to buybacks, EBITDA margin improving, a P/E ratio of 18, a 1% dividend yield and an 8.3% free-cash-flow yield, with a record $4 billion quarterly capital return. Guidance is high-single-digit to low-to-mid-teens growth, and as a fee business Booking gains from travel-price inflation. His conservative arithmetic gives roughly a 13% return (12% growth plus 1% dividend). The video then turns to AI: answers from DeepSeek and Gemini suggest disruption, not destruction - AI agents could take 5-10% of Booking's 10-20% platform fees, squeezing margins rather than killing the business. He draws a parallel with McCormick, whose brands face pressure from Walmart's Great Value private-label range, and warns investors may only see disruption clearly once the stock is already down another 50%. Despite the cheap valuation he concludes the risk/reward is simply not attractive and says plainly it is a risk he is not taking, so he takes no position; a recession hitting travel is an added risk. No share price is stated and no buy, hold or target is given.
